```{python}
#| echo: false
from _common import *
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

NOAA's Optimum Interpolation SST v2.1 is a quarter-degree daily
analysis from September 1981, one netCDF file per day. It is served
by NCEI over HTTPS and mirrored on AWS Open Data.

## One day over HTTPS

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
status_callout("oisst-ncei")
```

```{python}
#| error: true
dsn = ("/vsicurl/https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/sea-surface-temperature-optimum-interpolation/"
       "v2.1/access/avhrr/202501/oisst-avhrr-v02r01.20250103.nc")
if live("oisst-ncei"):
    day = xr.open_dataset(dsn, engine="gdalxarray")
    print(day)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
assert dsn == store("oisst-ncei")["dsn"]
```

```{python}
#| error: true
#| fig-cap: "OISST v2.1 for one day, read from NCEI over /vsicurl/."
if live("oisst-ncei"):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
    day["sst"].isel(time=0, zlev=0).plot(ax=ax, cmap="RdYlBu_r", vmin=-2, vmax=32)
    ax.set_title(str(day.time.values[0])[:10])
    plt.show()
```

## The same product on S3

The AWS mirror is a public bucket, read anonymously. `config_options=`
applies GDAL settings around the open and again around every later
lazy read, so they do not need to be set process-wide:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
status_callout("oisst-aws")
```

```{python}
#| error: true
dsn = ("/vsis3/noaa-cdr-sea-surface-temp-optimum-interpolation-pds/"
       "data/v2.1/avhrr/198109/oisst-avhrr-v02r01.19810930.nc")
if live("oisst-aws"):
    first = xr.open_dataset(dsn, engine="gdalxarray",
                            config_options={"AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST": "YES", "AWS_REGION": "us-east-1"})
    print(first["sst"].sel(lat=-42.875, lon=148.125, method="nearest").values.ravel())
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
assert dsn == store("oisst-aws")["dsn"]
```

## Forty-five years of one day

A multidimensional VRT can stitch every daily file into one
`(time, zlev, lat, lon)` array. Zipped, the whole record is one small
file on a GitHub release; the VRT refers to the daily files on AWS, so
the composition is `/vsizip/` over `/vsicurl/` for the recipe and
`/vsis3/` for the data.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
status_callout("oisst-mdim-zip")
```

```{python}
#| error: true
dsn = ("/vsizip//vsicurl/https://github.com/mdsumner/xrdbi/releases/download/latest/"
       "oisst-mdim.vrt.zip/oisst-mdim.vrt")
if live("oisst-mdim-zip"):
    rec = xr.open_dataset(dsn, engine="gdalxarray", config_options={"AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST": "YES"})
    print(dict(rec.sizes), str(rec.time.values[0])[:10], str(rec.time.values[-1])[:10])
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
assert dsn == store("oisst-mdim-zip")["dsn"]
```

Each 27 June, in a one-degree box off eastern Tasmania.

One caution first. `isel(time=mask)` with a sparse boolean or integer
selection is read by gdalxarray as one covering slab, from the first
selected day to the last, and thinned in memory afterwards. Across this
record that would open every daily file from 1982 to now to keep 45 of
them. Selecting one day at a time keeps each read to the day it needs:

```{python}
#| error: true
#| fig-cap: "Mean SST on 27 June each year, 43-44S 147-148E, off eastern Tasmania."
if live("oisst-mdim-zip"):
    t = rec.time.dt
    days = np.flatnonzero(((t.month == 6) & (t.day == 27)).values)
    box = rec["sst"].sel(lat=slice(-44, -43), lon=slice(147, 148))
    series = xr.concat([box.isel(time=int(i)).mean(["zlev", "lat", "lon"]).load()
                        for i in days], "time")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.5))
    series.plot(ax=ax, marker="o")
    ax.set_ylabel("SST (degrees C)"); ax.set_title("27 June, each year of the record")
    plt.show()
```
